assessment: The sample misses the course-set and handling-time targets. Assignment changes and renames correlate with affected exports, but neither the selection failure nor the handling bottleneck is established. The unsampled course split leaves an important isolation and identity case untested.

openings.claim: A center-authorized, week-specific course manifest could preserve export membership through instructor changes and renames while attendance entry continues. The manifest would pin course identity and expected membership, not freeze attendance records.
openings.delta: Move the coordinator's course-set check before CSV generation and make its result independent of the current instructor assignment.
openings.prediction: With the same attendance records, changing only current assignment or display name will leave manifest-based membership stable. A fabricated course split will expose whether identity continuity requires an explicit coordinator decision.
openings.probe: In staging, compare current selection and a manifest prototype on unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses. Have consenting coordinators identify intended membership, then measure total preparation plus checking time. Keep the documented CSV, enforce center authorization during extraction, and exercise concurrent attendance entry.
assumptions: Stable course identifiers exist or are inexpensive to introduce.
Coordinators can resolve weekly membership without costly timetable reconciliation.
Implementation fits six engineer-days and existing hosting.

openings.claim: Would immediate, authorized replacement exports remove most excess coordinator handling, or would checking and spreadsheet work remain the dominant cost?
openings.delta: Distinguish delay in obtaining a replacement from active handling and from incorrect course selection; faster delivery alone need not improve the stated median.
openings.prediction: If request-and-return interruptions drive handling, immediate replacement will reduce active minutes and repeated checking. If spreadsheet work dominates, elapsed waiting will shrink while active minutes remain similar.
openings.probe: Use paired fabricated export tasks in the two coordinator sessions, counterbalancing ordinary replacement requests and simulated immediate delivery. Record active checking, requesting, downloading and importing separately from waiting. Deliver only the existing CSV inside authorized workspaces; assess measured savings before implementing a bounded, rate-limited regeneration control.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate the relevant coordinator workflow.
Any subsequent implementation requires separate confirmation of six-day effort, hosting capacity and uninterrupted attendance entry.
